subject: Re: EdgeFin — Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology
messages:

Cc: Connor Obrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeFin — Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

- Business-level SLOs you called out:
  - P95 latency for interactive queries: <= 420ms (90% of traffic)
  - P99 tail latency target: <= 900ms (critical for UI)
  - Sustained throughput target: 2,000 requests/minute
  - Peak concurrency expected: 120 concurrent sessions
  - Streaming requirement: token-by-token delivery for live updates (client expects <50ms inter-token latency)

- Assumptions we discussed:
  - Average model context length ~ 1k tokens; typical prompt+response ~ 800 tokens
  - Mixture of short confirmations and longer multi-turn assistant responses
  - Sensitive data must stay in VPC / private deployment for initial pilot

Next steps (proposed):
1) We’ll share our benchmark methodology (prompt sets, harness, measurement definitions) so you can validate reproducibility.
2) You share any additional prompt variants / production traffic traces we should include (sanitized).
3) Run an initial benchmark on our Redwood Dedicated rig: 2-hour soak at expected concurrency, plus a streaming pass at lower concurrency to measure inter-token latencies.
4) Align on acceptance criteria and sign off for pilot run.

I’m attaching an initial methodology doc and a small sample prompt set you can use. Happy to walk through the harness live if you want — propose Wed 16th or Thu 17th for a 30-min workshop.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-benchmark-methods-v1.pdf (PDF, 240KB)]
[Attachment: edgefin_sample_prompts.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@edgefin.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeFin — Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- P95/P99 targets: the UI team is particularly sensitive to p99 spikes above 1s — can you confirm how you measure tail latency (server-side vs end-to-end including network)?
- Throughput: the 2,000 requests/min is steady-state; during rebalances we expect short bursts to ~3k/min for 5–10 minutes. Does your autoscaling accommodate that without warmup latency?
- Streaming: yes, streaming is mandatory for our quote flow. The client-side needs a predictable inter-token latency <50ms; if you could include a streaming-specific measurement we can validate client UX.

We’ll also attach two anonymized production traces (separately, security team will push to the shared drive) — they include token lengths and concurrency timestamps.

Would like the methodology doc to specify exact measurement definitions (how you compute P95/P99, sample sizes, warmup exclusion, error-handling). If you can include a reproducible harness (script + Dockerfile or a small k6 script), that would speed validation.

Samir
CTO, EdgeFin
[sent from mobile]

Samir —

Thanks — I’ve incorporated the clarifications into the methodology and attached the files you asked for. Highlights from the attached redwood-benchmark-methods-v1.pdf: 

- Measurement definitions:
  - P95/P99 are computed on server-side response completion time measured at the ingress load balancer (includes queuing + model inference, excludes client render time). We provide a small optional end-to-end probe you can run to include network.
  - Sample size: each percentile computed over a 15-minute window with at least 10k samples; longer runs for tail stability recommended.
  - Warmup: first 5 minutes excluded from steady-state measurements.
  - Error handling: retries are counted separately; error rate reported alongside latency buckets.

- Benchmark harness:
  - Dockerized harness + k6 script (instructions) to generate traffic patterns: steady-state, burst, and streaming flows.
  - Streaming test uses a WebSocket-based client sim that sends partial prompts and measures inter-token arrival times at the client. We record per-token latency and report median/inter-quartile/inter-decile for inter-token times.
  - Concurrency plan: sample scenario provided for ramp to 120 concurrent sessions and soak at 50/100/120 for 2 hours.

- Reproducibility:
  - We include the exact model config, quantization profile, runtime knobs, and the seed for any randomized prompt shuffling.
  - Results exported as CSV + a JSON summary (we attached sample outputs).

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-methods-v1.pdf, edgefin_sample_prompts.csv

Next steps: if this looks good, Connor and our infra team can schedule a time next week to run the harness against your VPC cluster or our Dedicated instance. Also happy to run the first pass ourselves and share raw metrics.

Best,
Marissa
